ADDITIONAL MACT, HARIHAR, AWARDING A COMPENSATION OF Rs.3,94,000/- WITH INTEREST 6% P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL DEPOSIT.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR DISMISSAL, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  NC: 2023:KHC:33086  MFA No. 9972 of 2012  JUDGMENT

This is an appeal filed by the insurance company aggrieved by the Award dated 19.06.2012 passed in M.V.C.No.61/2008 by the Senior Civil Judge & Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Harihar whereby the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.3,94,000/-.
2.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge & Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Harihar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.36,15,000/- for the death of the deceased in the accident.

The case of the claimant is that on 11.04.2006 at about 8:45 p.m.,
when claimant No.1 and the deceased were passing near Honnali bus-stand circle on The New India Assurance Co Ltd vs Sri H A Vijayakumar on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99738483/
2 Honnali-Tumminakatte Road at about 9:05 p.m., in front of Laxmi Metal Store, the lorry driven by the second respondent came from Shimoga road which was proceeding towards Tumminakatte road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the lorry against the deceased.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co Ltd vs Sri H A Vijayakumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As a result, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
3. It is stated that the second respondent is not the driver of the vehicle, but he is the cleaner of the vehicle.
The owner of the vehicle had entrusted the vehicle to RW.2 on the said date.
When RW.2 parked the lorry at Honnali to have a NC: 2023:KHC:33086 meal, at that time, he had asked the cleaner to stay in the lorry till he comes back.
But, the second respondent had taken the lorry and caused the accident.
4. It is the case of the insurance company that the second respondent himself is the driver of the vehicle to whom the owner had entrusted and he was not having a valid driving license.
It is the contention of the insurance company that there are violations of the terms and conditions of the policy and the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
5. The Court below considering the evidence of RW.2 who was the driver, according to the owner of the vehicle to whom he had entrusted the vehicle and Ex.
R.6 - the driving license shows that he was having a valid driving license.

The Court below had come to the conclusion that there is no violation of terms and conditions of the policy and if at all, the insurance company pleads that there are latches on the part of the owner, it is for the insurance company to substantiate the same by adducing cogent evidence.
As no other evidence is adduced, the Tribunal held that the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation and granted an amount of NC: 2023:KHC:33086 Rs.3,94,000/- as compensation.
Aggrieved thereby the insurance company is before this Court.

6. Learned counsel for the insurance company submits that even as per the police records also,
second respondent was traveling in the said vehicle and he was the driver of the vehicle who was not having a valid driving license.
When it is the case of no driving license, they are not liable to pay the compensation.
It is submitted that for the first time before the Tribunal, it is stated that the owner had entrusted the vehicle to RW.2 and the second respondent is the cleaner of the vehicle.
That story is put forth for the first time before the Tribunal.
He submits that the person who was driving the vehicle was not having a valid driving license and in that case, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
Alternatively, he submits that it is the evidence of RW.2 that when he went to have a meal, cleaner took the lorry.
It is stated that the driver was negligent in leaving the keys and letting a person, who was not having a driving license to drive the vehicle and caused the accident.
He submits that RW.2 is 70 years old and he was only having a driving license and they NC: 2023:KHC:33086 have cooked up such a story.
It is very much doubtful that a person of 70 years old can drive the lorry.
7. Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that they have not preferred any appeal against the order passed by the Tribunal.
He submits that in the light of the changed legal possession where the future prospects were not considered, even under the other heads, they would be entitled for more compensation.

This Act being a beneficial legislation without there being an appeal, this Court invoking Order 41, Rule 33 of C.P.C. can enhance the compensation and he relied The New India Assurance Co Ltd vs Sri H A Vijayakumar on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99738483/
3 on an order passed by this Court in M.F.A.No.8449/2015 dated 19.10.2022 where the similar arguments were addressed before the Court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Learned counsel appearing for the owner submits that there is no violation of terms and conditions of the policy and he had entrusted the vehicle to a person who was having a valid driving license.
The said person being the driver is examined and the driving license was placed on record.

He submits that the Court below relying on the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sohal Lal Passi V/s P. Sesh Reddy NC: 2023:KHC:33086 and others1 had held that the burden lies on the insurance company.

entities.text: Sohal Lal Passi V/s P. Sesh Reddy NC: 2023:KHC:33086 and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He had also relied on the Division Bench judgment of this Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd., Bangalore Vs. Smt. H.D.Nagarathnamma And Others2 wherein the Division Bench had taken a similar view that burden of proof is on the insurer who has raised plea and it is for the insurer to prove that insured by entrusting the vehicle to the person not holding license to drive the type of vehicle in question had deliberately committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., Bangalore Vs. Smt. H.D.Nagarathnamma And Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that in this case as the owner had entrusted the vehicle to a person who was having a driving license, there is no violation of the terms and conditions of the policy and as such the insurance company alone is liable to pay the compensation.
9. Having heard the learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.
The whole case of the insurance company is that second respondent is the driver of the vehicle to whom the owner had entrusted the vehicle and that person was not having a driving license.

It is submitted 1996 ACJ 1044 2001 (4) Kar.L.J. 566 (DB) NC: 2023:KHC:33086 that even as per the police records also second respondent is shown as the driver of the vehicle and as there is no driving license to him,
it amounts to violation of terms and conditions of the policy and they are not liable to pay the compensation.

Even if it is a case of the owner of the vehicle that at that relevant point of time,
second respondent was driving the vehicle, but second respondent is the cleaner and RW.2 was the driver of the vehicle and RW.2 was having a driving license.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the insurance company that he is aged 70 years and in all probability he cannot drive the vehicle.
That submission also has no legs to stand.
Even if there is any discrepancy between the case of the owner of the vehicle and the police records, the Court below would have considered all those aspects.
But even as per the police records also, at the relevant point of time, the second respondent was driving the vehicle.
Now, it is for the insurance company to prove that RW.2 had nothing to do with the vehicle.
The owner of the vehicle had never entrusted the vehicle to him.
But it is the second respondent who was entrusted the vehicle.
In that direction, except relying on the evidence of RW.2 and the case of the owner of the vehicle they NC: 2023:KHC:33086 have not chosen to take any steps or adduced any evidence.

In that view of the matter, the Court below relying on the judgment of the Apex Court had rightly held that there was no violation of terms and conditions of the policy and the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, this Court finds no reason to interfere with the finding of the Court below.
10. Learned counsel for the insurance company has also alternatively argued that the principle of pay and recover may be applied.
Even for applying the principle of pay and recovery, there should be lapses and latches on the part of the owner of the vehicle which in this case the insurance company could not establish.
In view of the same, even the question of applying pay and recover will also not arise.

sentences.text: Then coming to the contention of the learned counsel for the claimant that by considering order 41 Rule 33 of C.P.C., this Court can enhance the compensation without there being an appeal, no doubt the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation and there are judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court on either side, where one line of judgment observed that without there being an appeal still Court can enhance the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:33086 compensation and in the other line of judgment, the Apex Court had taken a view that without there being an appeal filed by the claimant, no such exercise can be done.
12. Coming to the facts of the case, this is an appeal filed by the insurance company questioning only the liability.

In case they questioned the quantum while adjudicating the same, if this Court comes to the conclusion that the compensation that was awarded by the Tribunal was not reasonable,
definitely, this Court would have gone into the said issue and pass appropriate orders.
But this appeal is purely on liability and this Court is not inclined to go into any of the said aspects.
13. Accordingly, the appeal of the insurance company is dismissed.
i. The amount that is deposited by the insurance company shall be forthwith transmitted to the Court below.
ii. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court records to the Tribunal along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
No costs.
14. Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
